title: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India

content.caseIdentity: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India, (1997) 3 SCC 261
content.facts: The case arose from a batch of matters concerning the constitutional validity and operation of the tribunal system created under Articles 323-A and 323-B, including challenges involving the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985. The central dispute concerned whether tribunal decisions could exclude or bypass the constitutional judicial-review and supervisory jurisdiction of the High Courts and the Supreme Court.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether Articles 323-A(2)(d) and 323-B(3)(d) and related statutory provisions could exclude judicial review by the High Courts under Articles 226 and 227 and by the Supreme Court under Article 32
Whether tribunals could function as substitutes for the constitutional judicial-review jurisdiction of the High Courts
content.ratioDecidendi: Judicial review by the High Courts under Articles 226 and 227 and by the Supreme Court under Article 32 forms part of the basic structure of the Constitution and cannot be excluded. Tribunals may perform their assigned adjudicatory functions, but their decisions remain subject to constitutional judicial review by the High Courts.
content.holding: Judicial review under Articles 32 and 226/227 is an inviolable basic structure feature; statutory tribunals cannot bypass or exclude High Court supervisory review under Article 226/227.
content.relevance: Established the constitutional position that tribunal decisions remain subject to High Court judicial review, while tribunals continue to exercise their statutory adjudicatory functions.
